A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LocalDPO work and contain readable main text and supplementary Sections 7–12. Equations, Algorithm 1, Tables 1–5 and Figures 1–12 can be matched despite layout changes and relocated references.

before.justification: v3 reports original VBench and VideoJAM experiments, loss and training-pair ablations, and human evaluations, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v4 retains the original benchmark experiments, ablations, human evaluations and supplementary qualitative results.

M1.justification: Sections 4 and 7 retain the same Bézier-mask generation, localized corruption, region-aware DPO loss and hybrid training objective. Algorithm 1 is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same curated Pexels video collection and VBench and VideoJAM text-to-video evaluations. No dataset, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the pretrained baseline, SFT, Vanilla DPO and DenseDPO for all three model configurations. The comparator sets in the main and supplementary human evaluations also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 5.2–5.4 retain the same metrics, model sizes, 165 VBench prompts, rank-64 LoRA, 540 training iterations, batch size 128 and inference settings. The user study still uses 20 participants and 50 sampled prompts.

E4.justification: The loss-component ablation in Table 3, preference-pair construction ablation in Table 4, convergence analysis in Figure 6 and supplementary corruption examples are retained without substantive revisions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. Existing seed information for generating comparison pairs is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain identical numerical results; for example, CogVideoX-2B LocalDPO's VBench aesthetic and imaging scores remain 0.6499 and 0.7080. Human-evaluation percentages, convergence curves and qualitative examples are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and objectives in Equations (1)–(6), including corruption-dependent weighting and mask-normalized errors, are unchanged. Algorithm 1 retains the same mathematical steps.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims of efficient preference-pair construction, localized preference learning and improved video quality and human preference. Editorial revisions do not alter their scientific scope.

C2.justification: The explanations of localized supervision, distribution-gap reduction and convergence are retained. Section 11 preserves the limitation that random masks lack semantic awareness and the proposed future use of detection and segmentation to guide them.

D1.justification: v4 newly provides a code-repository link and statement of code availability in the abstract. Hyperparameters, training settings, data-processing instructions and supplementary mask-generation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 removes nine background references, including Seedance 1.0, STIV, Make-A-Video and HOIGen-1M, reducing the bibliography from 82 to 73 entries. The central positioning against existing video preference-optimization methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 2 is condensed and polished, author contribution notes are updated, and a funding acknowledgment is added. Supplementary sections now precede the references, with their separate title heading removed; most prose and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: All figures and tables are retained, but several displays move: Tables 1–2 shift earlier and Algorithm 1 is placed beside its explanation. Caption emphasis, spacing and pagination change without substantive redesign of the displays.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves usability through the new code-access pointer, tighter related-work prose and better placement of Algorithm 1. The limitations discussion is also kept together instead of being interrupted across several pages. Background citation coverage narrows, but the central positioning and scientific evidence remain intact; the gains are primarily editorial and practical.
